content_voiceover: This table expands on the H. pylori story, showing that several bacteria are linked to specific extranodal marginal zone lymphomas based on where they infect. H. pylori itself is tied to gastric MALT lymphoma, but also more broadly to extranodal marginal zone lymphoma, diffuse large B cell lymphoma, and even Burkitt lymphoma. Borrelia burgdorferi, the Lyme disease organism, is linked to cutaneous MALT lymphoma. Chlamydophila psittaci is associated with ocular adnexal MALT lymphoma, the classic board pairing. In the lungs, organisms like Chlamydophila pneumoniae and Mycoplasma pneumoniae are linked to bronchial associated lymphoid tissue lymphoma, while Campylobacter jejuni is tied to IPSID, an intestinal lymphoproliferative disorder. Coxiella burnetii, the Q fever organism, has the broadest reach, associated with MALT lymphoma, diffuse large B cell lymphoma, follicular lymphoma, and even CLL. The exam pearl is to match the organism to its target organ, Chlamydophila psittaci with the eye, Borrelia with skin, and H. pylori with the stomach.
keypoints: H. pylori: gastric MALT lymphoma, the classic pairing
Chlamydophila psittaci: ocular adnexal MALT lymphoma
Coxiella burnetii: broadest association, including CLL and DLBCL
keypoint_voiceover: Match the organism to the organ for boards. H. pylori with gastric MALT lymphoma, Chlamydophila psittaci with ocular adnexal lymphoma, and Borrelia burgdorferi with cutaneous MALT lymphoma are the classic high yield pairings.
